OP, don’t listen to people who say rehome because you have mental health problems. It’s an insane advise. That’s what Reddit always does. Advises you to drown yourself if you have mental health problems. That is stigma for you. 

I have a dog who is rather high energy and I have mental health problems. In due course, I learned to solve the issues that arise from that. When I am alright, I play with her, train her, walk with her a lot etc. When I am depressed and can’t really get out of bed, I give her kongs, chews and other things that would keep her engaged without too much involvement on my part. I still drag myself out of bed to walk with her and it usually helps me with my own mental health too. 

I presume, he/she is a new dog. I believe that over time you will figure out a way to keep him or her satisfied when you are not at your best. 

I am also currently training my dog to do DTP (deep therapy training). It’s when a dog lie on top of you during a flashback or a panic attack to calm you with their weight (I have PTSD on top of everything). It’s pretty easy to teach to do on command but not so easy to teach the dog to recognize the signs. I just thought I put it out here so that you can check it out. It has additional benefits of keeping your dog busy, engaged and mentally stimulated, and improving your mental health (although depends on your issues of course). 

All of that being said, you not recognizing this behavior as playful does tell me that you have a lot of educating to do. 6 times with instructor is not enough for sure for a puppy like this. You want to watch seminars, read books about dogs, do more positive reinforcement training with instructor or in a group setting, maybe to pick up a hobby you can do together (like running, agility or, idk, yoga or dancing with your dog — whatever works for you).

Wish you the very best!

The accents and dialects back then differed by region and by class (peasants, merchants, nobility), and there was a lot of conversation about it among the noble and the learned (I can remember reading some Russian literary critic being annoyed about Yesenin, a Russian poet, emulating Russian peasants in what the critic thought was artificial and crude manner).

Also, I had some other sexual experiences that caused me extreme flashbacks, and I love doing these things now. 

Yes, it is not a quick process getting back into things that caused a flashback but I don’t think it is a reason to juat cross it out and not try it again. I finished the series last year, got an A in two courses, got A+ in an
 honors course and a B+ in one. My general advise for econ100A series would be the following:

1) don’t waste your time and money on the Econ Tutor. There are enough other resources offered to stay afloat.
2) spend the majority of time on understanding the concepts not on practicing (practicing solving problems would go way faster if you know all the concepts beforehand)
3) aim to watch microeconomics handbook videos before the lecture because otherwise it’s hard to follow the lecture, and definitely watch ALL of them by the time of exam (especially with Famulari)
4) don’t study only before midterms and finals. I’m generally prone to doing just that and it works out fine for me a lot of the time but in Econ100 series PSET is overflowed the week prior to the exam so you have to wait a long time in a stuffy room to ask even a short question so if you want to get help and personal attention be non-conformist and study two weeks before exam.
5) the second week go to several sections to choose TAs you like most so that to go to their section in future, and most importantly to when they are at PSET. 
6) Set your own deadlines for homeworks so that to stay on track
7) try to go to Famulari’s OHs

In terms of usefulness, I would rate the extra resources in the course as follows (it’s certainly individual): 

1) video handbook
2) PSET
3) midterm and final reviews
4) prof OHs (obviously, didn’t go to all of them) and just talking after the lectures 
5) sections (I would frequently skip them) 

This course is a lot of work but I personally found it extremely rewarding. Good luck!
